songs.title: Dangly Panther
songs.reason: Jimpster runs Freerange, the label that put out Milton Jackson and Shur-I-Kan — this is the house end of that roster, same warm Rhodes chords and shuffling live-feel drums.

similar_to.why: Freerange labelmates working the same deep, chord-led house template
Jimpster A&R'd and released Shur-I-Kan's records

songs.credit_connection: Jimpster founded Freerange Records, home of both Milton Jackson and Shur-I-Kan

songs.title: Beau Mot Plage
songs.reason: The record that made microhouse a genre — clipped guitar loops over a dubbed-out shuffle, the same fascination with texture-as-groove that runs through the Milton Jackson tracks.

similar_to.why: both German minimal/tech-house craftsmen working the same fine-grained percussion

songs.title: Rain
songs.reason: The deep-house vocal lineage Kings Of Tomorrow come out of — Chandler is the New Jersey source for that whole warm, gospel-inflected sound.

similar_to.why: same New Jersey deep-house lineage; Sandy Rivera and Chandler are direct peers

songs.influence_chain: Kerri Chandler -> Kings Of Tomorrow -> UK deep house

songs.title: Rej
songs.reason: The track that pulled deep house back toward melody in the mid-2000s — a single rolling bassline and one hook, held for eight minutes. Sits right beside the Milton Jackson material.

similar_to.why: same patient, chord-driven deep house built on one idea

songs.title: Raw Cuts #3
songs.reason: Danilo Plessow builds house out of chopped jazz and soul records, which is exactly the bridge between your St Germain and your Milton Jackson tracks.

similar_to.why: both build house from live jazz sampling rather than synths
shared crate-digging, live-instrument approach

verification.matched_artist: Danilo Plessow & Motor City Drum Ensemble
verification.claimed_as: Motor City Drum Ensemble — Raw Cuts #3

songs.title: Aquarium
songs.reason: Core Los Angeles beat scene — the same Low End Theory circle as Flying Lotus and Ras G, but sparser, with a lot of space left between the drums.

similar_to.why: both central to the Low End Theory / LA beat scene
same LA lineage of woozy, detuned instrumental hip hop

songs.influence_chain: Flying Lotus -> Low End Theory -> Nosaj Thing

songs.title: Lucid Waking
songs.reason: Signed to Flying Lotus's Brainfeeder and a Low End Theory regular — the same swung, off-grid drum programming as your Teebs and Ras G tracks.

similar_to.why: Brainfeeder labelmates with the same soft, collage-like beat construction
same Low End Theory circle

songs.credit_connection: Released on Brainfeeder, Flying Lotus's label

songs.title: FUSE
songs.reason: The Glasgow answer to the LA beat scene — maximalist where Teebs is minimal, but the same warped-sample, wrong-speed sensibility as your Lone tracks.

similar_to.why: both mine early-90s rave and R&B textures through a beat-scene lens

songs.title: Gunshotta
songs.reason: Footwork tempos wrapped in jungle breaks and pads — the natural next step from the Lone records, which chase the same rave nostalgia at a lower BPM.

similar_to.why: both rebuild early-90s hardcore and jungle as melodic listening music
shared post-dubstep UK sensibility

songs.title: I'm God
songs.reason: Blown-out, pitch-shifted vocal samples over cavernous reverb — the instrumental hip hop side of the same cloud that produced your oOoOO and Purity Ring tracks.

similar_to.why: same era of hazy, reverb-drenched instrumental hip hop
shared witch-house-adjacent atmosphere

songs.title: See Birds (Moon)
songs.reason: Tri Angle Records labelmate of oOoOO — the same pitched-down vocals and water-logged reverb, but built on field recordings rather than drum machines.

similar_to.why: Tri Angle labelmates who defined the witch house sound together
same era of pitched-vocal electronic pop

songs.credit_connection: Released on Tri Angle Records alongside oOoOO

songs.title: Brokendate
songs.reason: Deliberately degraded 80s synth textures at half speed — the polished end of the same nostalgia your Home tracks run on.

similar_to.why: both build warm, VHS-degraded synth music from the same 80s palette

songs.title: i was all over her
songs.reason: Bedroom recording that became a slow-burn internet standard — the same lo-fi, tape-saturated intimacy that made the Home and Foxes In Fiction tracks land.

similar_to.why: same bedroom-recorded, reverb-heavy dream pop
shared lo-fi internet-native aesthetic

verification.claimed_as: Salvia Palth — i was all over her

songs.title: Kiara
songs.reason: Simon Green remixed the Maya Jane Coles track in your playlist — this is his own work, the same live-instrument downtempo that connects your Thievery Corporation and Quantic picks.

similar_to.why: Bonobo produced the remix of this exact track in your playlist
same live-instrument downtempo lineage

songs.credit_connection: Bonobo remixed Maya Jane Coles' 'Something In The Air', which is in this playlist

songs.title: Tip Your Bartender
songs.reason: The post-hardcore record Deftones fans always end up at — same dynamic swing between whispered restraint and full-band detonation, with a far more elastic rhythm section.

similar_to.why: same quiet-to-violent dynamic and sung-screamed vocal contrast

songs.title: Fazer
songs.reason: The New York post-hardcore blueprint that Deftones and Glassjaw both built on — dense, mid-tempo, and rhythmically heavier than it is loud.

similar_to.why: Quicksand is a direct forerunner of the groove-heavy post-hardcore Deftones refined

songs.title: Mother Mary
songs.reason: Sacramento contemporaries of Deftones, and the missing link to Incubus's melodic side — Jonah Matranga sings where the genre expected a scream.

similar_to.why: same Sacramento scene and era, frequently toured together
shared melodic post-hardcore instincts

songs.title: Send the Pain Below
songs.reason: Exact contemporaries of Pressure 4-5 working the same drop-tuned, tightly produced early-2000s alt-metal, but with more melodic lift in the chorus.

similar_to.why: same 2001-2002 alt-metal wave and production sound

songs.title: So Good at Being in Trouble
songs.reason: Ruban Nielson records everything himself through deliberately cheap gear, which gives it the same slightly-wrong, sun-bleached quality as the Tame Impala tracks.

similar_to.album: Feels Like We Only Go Backwards
similar_to.why: both are one-man psych projects built on saturated, tape-warm home recording
shared woozy, detuned bedroom-psych sensibility

verification.matched_title: So Good at Being in Trouble
verification.claimed_as: Unknown Mortal Orchestra — So Good at Being in Trouble

songs.title: Sweep Me Off My Feet
songs.reason: Shares members with Tame Impala and is produced by Kevin Parker — literally the same Perth studio and the same hands on the desk, pushed further toward glam.

similar_to.album: The Less I Know The Better
similar_to.why: overlapping membership; Kevin Parker produced and mixed this record

songs.credit_connection: Produced by Kevin Parker of Tame Impala; the bands share members

verification.claimed_as: Pond — Sweep Me Off My Feet

songs.title: Car
songs.reason: The Pacific Northwest indie record Modest Mouse grew up on — same angular, unresolved guitar lines and the same refusal to land on an obvious chorus.

similar_to.why: Doug Martsch is the direct forerunner of Modest Mouse's Northwest indie sound

songs.influence_chain: Built to Spill -> Modest Mouse -> Northwest indie

songs.title: Two Weeks
songs.reason: Four-part harmony over a deliberately stiff piano figure — the same interest in odd arrangement and layered vocals that makes the Menomena track work.

similar_to.why: both build indie rock from unusual arrangements and stacked vocal harmony
shared art-pop approach to rhythm and voice

songs.title: 93 'til Infinity
songs.reason: The Bay Area answer to the Native Tongues records in your playlist — jazz loops, interlocking four-man verses, and no interest in menace.

similar_to.why: same jazz-sampling, posse-cut tradition
West Coast contemporaries with the same laid-back register

songs.title: The Choice Is Yours (Revisited)
songs.reason: Actual Native Tongues members — the same collective that produced De La Soul and A Tribe Called Quest, working the same loose, funny, sample-heavy formula.

similar_to.why: both core Native Tongues acts sharing producers and guest verses
same collective

songs.credit_connection: Black Sheep were members of the Native Tongues collective alongside De La Soul and A Tribe Called Quest

verification.claimed_as: Black Sheep — The Choice Is Yours (Revisited)

songs.title: Rebirth of Slick (Cool Like Dat)
songs.album: Reachin' (A New Refutation of Time and Space)
songs.reason: Built on an Art Blakey sample and delivered in a cool, conversational cadence — the jazz-rap counterpart to your Brubeck and Pharcyde picks in one track.

similar_to.why: same 1993 jazz-rap wave and unhurried delivery
the jazz vocabulary being sampled is exactly this era

verification.claimed_as: Digable Planets — Rebirth of Slick (Cool Like Dat)
